- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.

in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,

input.prompt:
I'm investigating why `andesim run --mode hybrid` is ~34x slower in wall-clock than `--mode cycle` for a tiny program (hello world), even though hybrid reports FEWER counted cycles (2734 vs 3573).

Repo: /home/nick/work/andesim. The C++ driver sources are under `src/` (entry `src/main.cpp`, hybrid orchestration likely `src/hybrid.cpp`/`src/cmd_run.cpp`/`src/run_plan.cpp`, process spawning `src/process.cpp`). The cycle-accurate vsim sources are NOT in this repo (they live in an external `hybrid_vsim` checkout); only the shared ABI is under `include/hybrid/`.

Answer these specific questions, with file:line evidence and short quotes:

1. In `--mode hybrid`, what processes does the driver spawn and in what order? Specifically: does it run a QEMU leg (qemu-system-riscv64 + the TCG plugin) to the entry trigger, then a SEPARATE vsim process that resumes and runs the ROI + drains? Or is it one combined process? Show the command lines / argv it builds for each leg.

2. In `--mode cycle`, what single process does it spawn (just vsim running the whole program)? Show the argv.

3. Where does the `window_cycles` / `[pc window_cycles] N (vsim mcycle=... - qemu mcycle=...)` line get printed, and how is it computed? Confirm it is the vsim mcycle delta around the ROI only.

4. Is there ANY existing per-phase timing, profiling, or verbose/debug flag (env var or CLI) in the driver that would print how long the QEMU leg vs the vsim leg took? Look for std::chrono, getenv, --verbose, --debug, ANDESIM_*, HYBRID_* env vars. List every relevant knob.

5. How could I run JUST the QEMU/handoff leg standalone (the developer escape-hatch), to time it separately from the vsim leg? Is there a documented way (a script, a subcommand, or an env var that stops after the drain)?

6. Does the hybrid vsim leg's argv differ from the cycle leg's argv in a way that would make it do extra work (e.g. enabling the Debug Module / JTAG / resume path, loading a state file, mapping a shared region)? Quote the differing flags.

Do NOT modify any files. Report concisely: a numbered answer to each question with file:line citations. If something isn't in this repo (e.g. the DMI restore loop lives in the external vsim repo), say so explicitly rather than guessing.

content.text:
Hybrid is slow because of the QEMU->vsim state-handoff ceremony, not the simulation. It is a roughly fixed cost (~26s here) that has almost nothing to do with your ROI size, and it never shows up in the cycle figure.

Measured just now on your `hello.elf`:

| run | counted cycles | wall-clock |
|---|---|---|
| `--mode cycle` (whole program on vsim) | 3573 | 0.79s |
| `--mode hybrid` (your run, main->_exit) | 2734 | 27.29s |
| QEMU fast-leg alone (reset->main, drain) | - | **0.08s** |

What this proves:
- The QEMU leg is **0.08s**. Negligible.
- vsim cold-runs the **entire** program (3573 cycles, more than your ROI) in **0.79s**. So simulating everything hello does costs under 1 second.
- The hybrid vsim leg therefore spends `27.29 - 0.08 ~= 27.2s`, of which only ~0.6s is the ROI. The other **~26s is the resume + drain handoff**.

Why the handoff is expensive: `--resume-from-qemu` makes vsim write every GPR/FPR/CSR (and V-state if used) into the **halted** hart through the RISC-V Debug Module (abstract commands + program buffer), and `--handoff-out` reads them all back the same way. Each register access clocks the Verilator RTL through the slow debug-module/JTAG handshake. Those cycles run with the hart halted, so they burn real wall-clock but never advance `mcycle`. That is exactly why you see a tiny cycle number (2734) next to a huge wall time.

When hybrid actually wins: hybrid trades "simulate the pre-ROI region on vsim" for "pay the fixed handoff cost." For hello, the pre-ROI region is only ~839 cycles (3573 - 2734), so you save under 1s of vsim time but pay ~26s of handoff. Net loss. Hybrid only pays off when the part you skip in QEMU (boot, big data load, long warm-up) is **millions+ of cycles** - then skipping it on vsim saves far more than the handoff costs. For a tiny program like hello, use `--mode cycle`.

One side note worth a separate look: a near-empty ROI (`--pc-end 0x100076`) still reported **2728** cycles, basically the same as the full ROI. That suggests the `pc-end` may not be taking effect (likely clamped/ignored), so the cycle figure for very short PC windows may not mean what you expect - but that is a correctness question, separate from the speed one you asked about.
